capabilities: Insert HTML tables from a hover grid with an optional header row
Merge, split, insert, and delete rows, columns, and cells
Set borders, alignment, shading, and column widths per table, row, column, or cell
Insert and resize vault images inside table cells
Reformat hand-edited tables back into the canonical one-cell-per-line layout
disambiguation: Edits real HTML <table> markup, not Markdown pipe tables, and Obsidian's native table controls and Advanced Tables ignore its output.
extras: Sister plugin to HTML Font Toolbar: both work independently but stack and namespace their CSS when installed together. README warns HTML tables render unstyled or not at all on GitHub, Hugo, and Pandoc, and that Markdown inside HTML blocks is not processed, making this best for build-once reference tables rather than working documents.
problem: Markdown pipe tables in Obsidian cannot merge cells, style individual cells, hold multi-block content, or center themselves, so structural table edits require tedious hand-written HTML.
summary: Word-style toolbar that creates and edits real HTML tables in notes, with merged cells, per-row borders, shading, alignment, and images inside cells.
